title: Reconciliation Worksheet for the Latest Estimated Month — Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage
content:
The worksheet below fixes, for Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage, the reconciliation reduction on the latest month billed as an estimate once the case is approved.

**A. The month.** The month reconciled is the latest service month for which the case carries a patient pay charge billed as an estimate (charge basis "estimated pending"), on a case in status eligible. On a case in any other status the reduction is zero.

**B. Estimates billed for the month.** The amount of the month's patient pay charges billed as estimates less the reductions already posted for that service month.

**C. The patient pay the notice sets for the month.** The patient pay on the case's current notice when that notice took effect on or before the first day of the month (a current notice with no effective date recorded counts as taking effect after the first day of the month); when the current notice took effect after the first day of the month, the amount of the notice-basis charge (charge basis "actual notice") billed for the month that follows the reconciled month — the amount the earlier notice set — or the current notice amount where no such charge was billed.

**D. When the month is priced day by day.** The month is priced day by day where a pending accrual is posted for the month, the bed-hold days booked for the month all belong to one bed-hold reservation, the month's Part A days were all booked by the resident's coverage with the latest coverage start, and every day of the month is accounted for once: the days in the center that the month's pending accrual counts, the bed-hold days booked for the month less the days reversed from those bookings, the days with no bed held, the days before a skilled admission inside the month and the days after a held bed's last held day inside the month where the hospital discharged the resident elsewhere add up to the month's calendar days. For this count, the days with no bed held are, as far as they fall in the month: from the leave start of the resident's latest reservation in status declined (by leave start); after the last held day of the resident's latest reservation that ended because the payer's reserved days were used with no private extension (by end date); after the release of the resident's latest reservation in status released (by release date); and after the last held day of the resident's latest private hold that ended unpaid or at its maximum (by end date; where one of each shares the latest end date, the one that ended unpaid) — each up to the day before its return, or to the month's end where the resident has not come back. A skilled admission is the resident's Medicare coverage with the latest coverage start date beginning inside the month on the day its qualifying hospital stay ended; the held bed is the resident's reservation with the latest end date among those that ended because the hospital discharged the resident elsewhere.

**E. Cost of care of a month not priced day by day.** The days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate, rounded half up to the cent, the days in the center being those the month's pending accrual counts, or every calendar day where no accrual was posted; a month of admission, discharge or death takes its patient pay under the partial-month rule (the lesser of the monthly patient pay and the days in the center times the Medicaid daily rate).

**F. Cost of care of a month priced day by day.** Every calendar day of the month priced at the Medicaid daily rate on the case, except that the Part A days Medicare covers in full (days booked for the month in benefit days 1 through 20, less the days reversed from those bookings) and the days a lapsed physician certification leaves to the center (days reversed as uncertified days from the month's bookings) carry no cost, and the Part A coinsurance days (days booked for the month in benefit days 21 through 100, less the days reversed from those bookings) are priced at the highest daily coinsurance booked for them. The days at the daily rate are the calendar days not taken out and not priced as coinsurance days, never fewer than zero; each kind of day is priced and rounded half up to the cent, and the priced kinds are added.

**G. Actual patient pay and the reduction.** The actual patient pay of the month is the lesser of C and the month's cost of care. The reconciliation reduction is the estimates billed for the month less the actual patient pay of the month, never below zero, rounded half up to the cent. Where two records share the latest date a reading goes by, the one posted first is read.

**Worked lines (hypothetical inputs).** A 31-day month; Medicaid daily rate 263.10 dollars; estimates billed 1,640.00 dollars; notice patient pay 1,402.55 dollars, effective before the month. Case one is priced day by day: a skilled stay whose benefit days 1 through 20 fall on days 1 to 20, after which Part A coverage ended. Case two is a month of admission not priced day by day, whose pending accrual counts 5 days in the center.

| Line | Case one | Case two |
|---|---|---|
| Part A days covered in full | 20 | not read |
| Days priced at the daily rate | 11 | 5 (days in the center) |
| Cost of care | 2,894.10 | 1,315.50 |
| Actual patient pay (lesser of notice amount and cost of care) | 1,402.55 | 1,315.50 |
| Reduction (estimates billed less actual patient pay) | 237.45 | 324.50 |
